records.finding: The framework maintains revisable problem, representation, hypothesis, evidence and intervention state and distinguishes predictions from observations. Its GALILEO section explicitly includes specialized human-executed assays and limits general-purpose discovery claims. The manuscript correctly uses this as a coupled-system architecture and failure-attribution principle, without borrowing therapeutic success as banking evidence.

DISCERN has 203 canonical tasks (79/102/22), eight tracks and eight primary models; levels are independently instantiated and scored. Counterfactual dossiers require conflict with elicited model priors. Perfect-score rates 60.8/34.2/0.6 percent match the source and are rubric-specific, with different denominators. The manuscript correctly excludes an end-to-end discovery interpretation and local reproduction.

Augur prunes pairs by Spearman rank correlation, elicits directed/confounded/spurious judgments, repairs cycles, selects stable/grounded narratives and trains a student for downstream trend prediction. F1/AUROC concern forecasting; causal sufficiency and missed nonlinear/lagged relations remain stated limits. The manuscript correctly distinguishes internal graph/narrative agreement from intervention identification.

The methodological workflow constructs diagrams from the assumptions actually used, retains multiple models, checks identification/testable implications and distinguishes missing relations from missing variables. The manuscript accurately treats this as a method for inspecting study assumptions rather than a verified LLM discovery implementation.

The review explicitly distinguishes confounders/colliders/mediators, discusses measurement error and asks whether text can encode several roles. It warns that semi-synthetic metadata can be chosen to favor recovery by the proposed method. The manuscript correctly motivates fixed clocks, independent adverse generators and comparison of text measurements without claiming that richer representations eliminate confounding.

The codebook g defines the textual outcome estimand; searching for g on estimation units risks induced dependence and overfitting. The paper separates discovery and estimation using training/test samples and imposes additional sufficiency for text treatments. The manuscript accurately transfers this to frozen model/prompt/retrieval/measurement rules while retaining target dependence on g.

The inconsistency metric is based on conflicting causal ratings; retrieval receives a mocked true graph, and debate adds opposed roles and an arbiter. The conclusion explicitly says reduced inconsistency does not imply accurate causal prediction and requests true-graph validation. The manuscript preserves this negative distinction instead of adopting the title as an elimination guarantee.

CausalPulse describes semantic services, domain-rule constraints, planning and MCP/A2A orchestration. Operational completion is distinct from root-cause attribution: PSE Hits@1=.44, precision=.46, recall=.40 and F1=.39 use manually annotated immediate-variable changes. The manuscript accurately distinguishes those annotations and local manufacturing operations from interventional truth or bank runtime.

The log-determinant acyclicity characterization is defined on W with spectral radius of its entrywise square below s; the nonsingular M-matrix domain is essential for the nonnegative zero-if-DAG result. The manuscript formula and cycle-series explanation preserve this domain and do not treat a log absolute determinant outside it as equivalent.

The original LiNGAM model is linear and acyclic with independent continuous non-Gaussian disturbances, causal sufficiency and repeated independent observations under a common model. Its algorithm uses ICA and ordering/normalization. The manuscript correctly separates that source result from the later DirectLiNGAM implementation, whose code requires separate nonpaper review.
